correctness.rationale: For all integers \(n\ge3\) invertible in the ground field, \(3n\) geometric components and \(n^2+3\) ordinary multiple points give a connected branch-incidence graph. The explicitly specified \(3n+n^2+2\) edges constitute a Galois-invariant spanning tree: \(3n\) family-star edges and \(n^2\) A-to-triple edges make three acyclic components, joined by two rational \(M_{1,1}\) edges. Every other B/C-to-triple edge is a chord indexed by a nonidentity pair of n-th roots of unity. Their fundamental cycles form an integral basis permuted without sign by Galois, proving the exact character module \(\mathbb Z[S]^{\oplus2}\) and hence the two Weil restrictions. The finite-field classification follows from fixed-point cardinalities \(\gcd(n,q^r-1)^2\) and Möbius inversion. Package verifier.py directly reconstructs trees and actions in 128 cases and checks the known normalization count over prime and extension fields; these finite tests are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The asserted NEW result is only the all-field, all-residue-class integral Picard-torus quotient. The directly inspected existing odd-degree Ceva work already proves the special q congruent +1 or -1 classes for odd \(n\ge5\) and \(p>n\); those are excluded as new results. The directly inspected twisted-triangular Fermat work already gives the complete point-count and zeta formulas (including the untwisted case); those are expressly background cross-checks. Neither source determines a Galois-permutation torus lattice for all Frobenius orders. value.rationale: The natural Fermat–Ceva line arrangements form an unbounded, geometrically distinguished family; an exact isomorphism of the arithmetic Picard torus, not only the zeta function, determines the finite-field group of torus points in every residue class. The invariant integral cycle basis is a structural lemma valid over arbitrary tame-characteristic fields. It settles previously missing higher-order and even-degree Frobenius classes rather than an arbitrary small parameter slice. The cubic and mixed split/quadratic cases visibly add arithmetic structure beyond the already-known point counts. No new value is attributed to the old zeta or geometry formula.
